proposals: NPCI should publish monthly UPI person-to-merchant volume and value for the fuel-retail category, so the digital share of forecourt payments — which this post found no authoritative source for, forcing a 30–90% grid — can be measured directly.

The Finance Ministry and NPCI should publish, six months after the 15 October 2026 MDR takes effect, fee collections by category, including the flat ₹5 charged on fuel transactions, so the actual incidence of the new fee can be compared with the scenarios debated before it was notified.

PPAC should decompose the dealer commission in its Ready Reckoner price build-up into its cost components, stating whether any allowance for payment-acceptance costs is included, so the question this post could not settle is answered from the formula itself.

IOCL, BPCL and HPCL should publish an outlet-coded list of their retail outlets offering cash withdrawal through Cash@PoS, micro-ATM or UPI-ATM, since only 18 of SBI's 693 listed fuel stations could be matched to a specific outlet and cash-out at pumps cannot currently be audited.

The RBI should publish ATM and white-label ATM counts by rural, semi-urban, urban and metropolitan population group every quarter, so the rural share of cash machines is a published number rather than a characterisation of where white-label operators deploy.
